sources.note: All four personas ran. A persona holds an issue when their first-pass verdict was a difficulty and their opinion after testing was unchanged, hardened or softened; where the one test proposed could not be executed (opinion not recorded), the first-pass verdict is carried as held and the element is provisional. A difficulty verdict with no test proposed and no opinion (complaints recorded only as out of scope) is not a purpose issue. Severity Low is assigned where only personas hold the issue and testing softened every holder's position. Detection false positives are counted under found_by 'none'.

screen1-a1.appearance: red and yellow striped flag with a numeral beside it
screen1-a1.description: flag picture with a count beside it, first item of the top bar
screen1-a1.issue_source: classified by se-tester from persona feedback
screen1-a1.classification_basis: Gopal: cue "The Spanish flag. The number 1 tells me nothing."; why "The flag suggests Spanish, but nothing says what pressing it does, and a bare '1' is a figure I would have to remember the meaning of."; solution "A word beside it, such as 'My courses' or 'Change course'."; after trying: softened. Read as Missing Purpose: their words describe being given nothing that says what it does — their cue names only a picture or 'nothing', and their fix asks for a word to be added.

tester.deciding_evidence: the flag opened the course panel, which is what the language-flag convention promises

personas.expectation: I think it opens something about my Spanish course, maybe a list to switch course. I do not know what the 1 is counting.
personas.cue: The flag means Spanish. Nothing tells me what the 1 means or that pressing it opens anything.
personas.why: A flag and a bare number. The flag I can name; the number has no unit and no label, so I cannot tell if this is a course switcher, a level, or a score.
personas.solution: Put a word next to the number, for example 'Spanish - Score 1', and make it look like something that opens a list (a small down arrow).

personas.expectation: I suppose it has to do with my Spanish course, perhaps it lets me choose or change the course. What the number 1 means I cannot say.
personas.cue: The Spanish flag. The number 1 tells me nothing.
personas.why: The flag suggests Spanish, but nothing says what pressing it does, and a bare '1' is a figure I would have to remember the meaning of.
personas.solution: A word beside it, such as 'My courses' or 'Change course'.

personas.expectation: I think it shows which language course I am on, and pressing it might let me change course. The '1' I cannot place: a level, a score, or a count.
personas.cue: The flag and the number 1. There is no word.
personas.why: I recognise that it is a flag, but I have to work at pictures, and the '1' could mean three different things. I would read it over and over without committing.
personas.solution: Put the word 'Spanish' or 'My courses' under it, and say what the 1 is, for example 'Score 1'.

personas.expectation: Opens something about my Spanish course, maybe lets me switch course. The 1 might be my level.
personas.cue: The flag. The 1 means nothing to me.
personas.why: The flag says Spanish, fine, but the 1 is a mystery number and nothing says 'switch course'.
personas.solution: Put a tiny down-arrow next to the flag so I know it opens a list, and a word under the number.

screen1-a1.disagreement_note: the tester tested it and found it clear (the flag opened the course panel, which is what the language-flag convention promises); Gopal held "navigate with difficulty" (The flag suggests Spanish, but nothing says what pressing it does, and a bare '1' is a…)
screen1-a1.recommendation: no tester recommendation (tester verdict Clear Purpose); persona suggestions — Gopal: "A word beside it, such as 'My courses' or 'Change course'."

screen1-a2.appearance: grey flame outline with a numeral beside it
screen1-a2.description: flame outline with a count beside it in the top bar

tester.deciding_evidence: nothing visible names the control before it is tapped; only the page it opens says 'Streak'
tester.recommendation: add a visible word under the glyph, e.g. 'Streak: 1 day', so the count and the destination are named

personas.expectation: Probably opens a page about a streak count. I am inferring 'streak' from the convention of flames in games, not from anything written.
personas.cue: A flame picture and a number. No word.
personas.why: A flame does not literally mean 'days in a row'. It is a metaphor (keeping a fire going). The number has no unit. It is also grey, which could mean disabled or could mean 'not done today' - I cannot tell which.
personas.solution: Write '1 day streak' or at least 'days' next to the number. Explain what grey means.

personas.expectation: I have no idea. A flame means fire to me. It might be a count of something.
personas.cue: Only the grey flame and the number 1.
personas.why: A flame is not a symbol I know in this setting, and there is no word to tell me what it counts or what happens if I press it.
personas.solution: Put a plain label under it, for example 'Days in a row: 1', and say what pressing it opens.

personas.expectation: No idea really. Perhaps a count of days of something; a flame does not tell me what.
personas.cue: A grey flame and the number 1, both very faint.
personas.why: A flame is not a word I can hold on to. Nothing tells me what the 1 counts or what pressing it would open, and the grey makes it look switched off.
personas.solution: A word beside it, such as '1 day streak', and a clear statement of what opens when I press it.

personas.expectation: Shows my streak - how many days in a row I've practised.
personas.cue: The flame. Every habit app uses a flame for a streak.
personas.why: Flame plus a number is a streak. I got it in a second.

screen1-a2.recommendation: add a visible word under the glyph, e.g. 'Streak: 1 day', so the count and the destination are named

personas.expectation: It tells me which lesson I am on. Pressing it might open that unit or tell me more about it.

personas.expectation: I think it tells me where I am in the course. If I pressed it, maybe it would show me the unit or let me pick another unit. I am not sure it is a button at all.

personas.why: The words tell me where I am, which I value a great deal, but it looks like a heading, not a button. I cannot tell whether pressing it does anything or what.
